clones.name: ngram
clones.what_they_ship: A source-aware AI video system for product and marketing teams that researches a source, storyboards, scripts, voices over, and produces on-brand business videos.

features.value: Accepts release notes, PDFs, prompts, URLs, product docs, screen recordings, and messy ideas as source material.
Handles research, storyboarding, scripting, and voiceover while keeping the user in control.
Video types include auto explainer, product launch, changelog, feature announcement, customer onboarding, sales enablement, tutorial/how-to, social clip, and teaser/trailer.
Basic includes unlimited manual video edits and 720p exports; Premium includes 1080p exports; Ultimate includes 4K exports, BrandKits, custom voices, and custom avatars.
Paid plans include unlimited manual editing and exports.

clones.how_the_ui_works: The landing page presents a source/input-first flow: provide a document, URL, prompt, recording, or idea, choose a video type or style/voice/avatar options, then review the generated business video.
clones.pipeline: Ingest source material, research it, generate storyboard/script/voiceover, produce an on-brand video, then use unlimited manual editing on paid plans and export/host it.
clones.pricing: Free is offered via Try ngram free; Basic is $29/month ($23.20/month annual, 20% off) with 3,000 credits and 720p exports; Premium $59/month ($47.20 annual) with 10,000 credits and 1080p; Ultimate $299/month ($239.20 annual) with 50,000 credits and 4K; Enterprise custom.
clones.clone_this: Clone the source-aware business-video pipeline: source ingestion, research, storyboard/script/voiceover, video-type presets, BrandKits, and manual revision.
clones.beat_this: Beat it with frame-level editing, faster social-first templates, and more explicit short-form clipping; an ngram comparison article identifies its trade-off as less frame-level control.

clones.name: OpenCut
clones.what_they_ship: A free/open-source editor project being rewritten from the ground up for web, desktop, and mobile; the README says the classic version is the one to use today.

features.value: Planned Editor API
Plugin-first architecture with first-class third-party plugins
One Rust-core codebase targeting desktop, mobile, and browser
Planned MCP server, headless automation/batch rendering, and in-editor scripting tab
MIT license

clones.how_the_ui_works: The fetched README does not describe the rewrite’s editor panels or timeline UI; it directs users to the classic version for current use.
clones.pipeline: The rewrite is described as a Rust core with web/api/desktop development commands; planned headless mode is intended for automation and batch rendering. The page does not state a shipped media-processing/export pipeline.
clones.pricing: No product pricing is stated; the project is MIT-licensed.
clones.clone_this: Clone the rewrite’s plugin-first, cross-platform architecture and planned Editor API/MCP/headless surfaces, while treating the current editor as not ready and directing users to the classic version.
clones.beat_this: Beat it with a currently usable editor, documented timeline/media pipeline, and explicit export behavior; the README itself says the rewrite is unfinished and classic is the current choice.

clones.name: YumCut
clones.what_they_ship: An open-source, self-hosted AI short-video generator for TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Instagram Reels that turns an idea into script, voice, visuals, captions, and a ready-to-post 9:16 edit.

features.value: Bearer-key User API for project creation, token quotes, status polling, stop/cancel, settings/catalog access, and final-media download URLs
Faceless-style vertical production and multilingual versions
Bring-your-own providers and local components where possible
Separate app and storage modes with signed upload/delete grants and typed API boundaries
Export-ready TikTok/Reels/Shorts output

clones.how_the_ui_works: The fetched pages describe a web app and an API rather than a detailed editor canvas layout; the API manages projects end to end and exposes final media download URLs.
clones.pipeline: Idea → generated script → voice → visuals → captions → final 9:16 video; external automation can quote token costs, create projects, poll status, cancel work, and fetch final media URLs.
clones.pricing: Personal use is stated as free. Hosted YumCut.com exists; commercial hosting/selling access requires a commercial license. The README says generation can be around 10x cheaper depending on stack/providers, not a fixed price.
clones.clone_this: Clone the end-to-end vertical generator, self-host/BYO-provider economics, and automation-first User API.
clones.beat_this: Beat it with a visible, fine-grained timeline editor and clearer fixed pricing/usage disclosure; YumCut’s fetched README emphasizes generation/API workflows rather than canvas editing or fixed rates.

clones.name: OpenReel Video
clones.what_they_ship: A fully client-side browser video editor and open-source CapCut alternative.

features.value: Unlimited multi-track timeline
Frame-accurate scrubbing, cut/trim/split/ripple delete, transitions, effects, blend modes, and 0.25x–4x speed
Rich text, 20+ text animations, karaoke subtitles, SVG/stickers, and keyframes
Audio mixing/effects, beat detection, ducking, and noise reduction
Color wheels/HSL/curves/LUTs
MP4, WebM, ProRes, audio and image-sequence export; custom settings, hardware encoding, progress/cancel
Screen recording, SRT import, project import/export, autosave/undo

clones.how_the_ui_works: Multi-track timeline, real-time preview, scrubbing, track management, snapping, shortcuts, and autosave are named; a complete panel layout is not described.
clones.pipeline: On-device React/TypeScript editing uses WebGPU rendering, WebCodecs decoding/encoding, frame caching, and Web Workers; exports include MP4/WebM/ProRes.
clones.pricing: Free forever; MIT licensed; no subscriptions or watermarks.
clones.clone_this: Clone the privacy-first browser-native multi-track editor and broad local export stack.
clones.beat_this: Beat it with a production-ready (rather than Beta) status, collaboration, and nested-sequence/export breadth.

clones.name: ArcReel
clones.what_they_ship: An open-source self-hosted AI video-production workspace for drama/novel adaptation, narrated shorts, ads, and product shorts, with editable video or Jianying draft export.

features.value: Content analysis/project planning and character/scene/prop assets
Structured scripts and storyboard/grid-storyboard stages
Reference reuse, review/regenerate, and rollback
Configurable text/image/video/TTS providers with cost estimates and usage tracking
Final composition and mainland-China Jianying draft export
Agent orchestration with user review
AGPL-3.0 plus NOTICE terms

clones.how_the_ui_works: Stages can be Agent-orchestrated or reviewed/adjusted/regenerated; a conventional NLE panel layout is not enumerated.
clones.pipeline: Source novel/screenplay/product assets → analysis/planning → assets → structured script → storyboard → clips/voice-over → final composition or Jianying draft. Recovery is conditional on provider progress lookup and recorded task ID.
clones.pricing: No pricing or paid tiers are stated; PRODUCT.md explicitly says such materials do not yet exist. Commercial deployment/white-labeling requires contact.
clones.clone_this: Clone the staged inspectable pipeline, provider abstraction, cost tracking, human review, and Jianying handoff.
clones.beat_this: Beat it with verified CapCut compatibility, a simpler NLE edit surface, and clearer pricing; CapCut compatibility is explicitly unverified and the product is single-admin self-hosted.

clones.name: QMedia
clones.what_they_ship: An open-source multimodal AI content search engine for creators, not a video editor.

features.value: Search image/text/short-video materials
Source-rich content cards and breakdowns
Multimodal RAG Q&A using image style, text layout, transcription, and summaries
Local/offline private-data search and Q&A
CLIP/BGE embeddings, Faster Whisper transcription, Ollama switching
Separate web, RAG, and model services
Short-video editing is a future plan

clones.how_the_ui_works: The UI is described as XHS-web-inspired content cards built with Next.js, TailwindCSS, and Shadcn/UI; no timeline UI is described.
clones.pipeline: Separate model services process assets; RAG retrieves/decomposes content and presents sources/answers in cards. Editing remains future work.
clones.pricing: No pricing is stated; MIT licensed.
clones.clone_this: Clone multimodal search, evidence cards, local deployment, and replaceable model services as an intelligence layer.
clones.beat_this: Beat it by shipping timeline editing, assembly, and export; the README lists editing under Future Plans.

clones.name: pyJianYingDraft
clones.what_they_ship: A lightweight Python tool for generating Jianying drafts, template editing, and version-dependent automated export.

features.value: Local video/image/audio timing and speed
Keyframes, masks, chroma key, backgrounds, blend modes
Stickers, audio fades/effects, tracks, animations, effects, filters, transitions
Text styles/animations, bubbles/WordArt, wrapping, SRT import
Template duplication, asset/text replacement, track import, metadata extraction
Batch export path/resolution/framerate on supported older Jianying

clones.how_the_ui_works: It has no own editor UI: it generates a draft that the user opens in Jianying; template mode loads/duplicates Jianying drafts.
clones.pipeline: Python writes Jianying drafts from local media and changes template assets/text/tracks; export automation controls Jianying and is OS/version limited. Windows supports all; Linux/macOS do not support automatic export.
clones.pricing: No pricing is stated; pip installation is documented.
clones.clone_this: Clone the draft-as-interchange/template replacement mechanic and structured Jianying effects/caption access.
clones.beat_this: Beat it with a self-contained cross-platform renderer/UI and modern compatibility: newer Jianying may require fallback_loader and automatic export generally fails on version 7+.

Platform-aware Shorts gate with nine structural/caption rules
Word-timestamp captions, normalization, delivery QA, audio/A-V and caption-sync checks
Interview invite/plan/build with source-gated guest data
Self-contained ffmpeg demos and contract tests

clones.pricing: No pricing is stated; no paid tiers are described.
clones.clone_this: Clone evidence-first fail-closed gates, deterministic contract, shared filter registry, and platform-aware automation.
clones.beat_this: Beat it with a visual timeline/editor, consumer onboarding, and integrated provider/export paths; the README presents a CLI/framework requiring an Editkin structured tool environment.

clones.beat_this: Beat it with automatic captions/scene assembly and a lower-input local-shop flow; the fetched page foregrounds manual NLE controls and does not name auto captions or URL ingestion.

steals.value: Ship a 9:16 portrait project by default, while allowing one source project to export 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1; make the canvas choice an early, visible control.
Accept the shop’s local video/still assets and a pasted YouTube or product URL: the input surface should be one short form, not a multi-app ingest chore.
Run the first pass automatically: choose highlights, trim silences, add beat-aware cuts, captions, background removal/reframe and a branded music bed, then leave a human review checkpoint.
Use a hybrid editor: transcript/text edits for fast copy changes plus a conventional multitrack timeline/canvas for deterministic trim, layers, captions and overlays.

Hand off an editor-neutral package every time: H.264 MP4 for immediate posting, SRT for caption portability, and an editable project package; add Jianying/CapCut-compatible draft generation when the shop uses that editor.
Make no-watermark 1080p output the free baseline and expose resolution, frame rate and format before render rather than after a paywall.
Use local-first/browser processing where possible, with hardware-accelerated render and project autosave so a small shop can keep its media private and continue without a heavyweight install.
Add evidence-first, fail-closed delivery QA: inspect caption sync, dead air, audio/A-V, flicker, B-roll coverage and platform framing before calling the clip done.
Persist a shop BrandKit—logo, colors, fonts, intro/outro—and apply it across captions, lower thirds and all aspect-ratio exports.
Expose an API/webhook path that can create a project, poll status, cancel work and return the final media URL for repeatable local-business campaigns.

do_not_copy.value: Do not make the free tier a watermark trap or silently cap it at low resolution: VEED explicitly describes free exports as watermarked and 720p.
Do not hide the core short-video workflow behind opaque credits, add-ons or tier-specific quality; make the exact output contract and remaining credits visible before generation.
Do not ship MP4-only when the user needs to continue editing: preserve SRT and an editable project/draft interchange path.

Do not force a local shop into a desktop-only, pro-post workflow for a simple Reel; Premiere and Resolve expose powerful professional stacks, but their pages foreground subscription/Studio tiers and multi-page finishing complexity.
Do not turn the first screen into asset sludge: KineMaster advertises 75,000+ assets across 10,000+ packs, a choice load that should be replaced by a few outcome-led presets.
Do not use creator counts, ratings or “viral” language as a substitute for a measurable input→edit→output workflow; require a file contract and QA evidence.
Do not present an unfinished editor rewrite as production-ready: OpenCut’s README says the rewrite is not ready and directs users to the classic version.
Do not label a search/RAG utility as an editor: QMedia lists short-video editing as a future plan, so it is an intelligence layer rather than a shipped timeline/export product.
Do not clone competitor branding or build a generic clone-brand; copy the observable mechanics (9:16, captions, handoff and QA) and differentiate on deterministic local-shop delivery.

clone_recipe:
1. Rebuild the prospect’s first-run surface as a single “make a shop short” form: accept a local video or stills plus an optional YouTube/product URL, collect one offer/CTA and brand kit, and create a 9:16 project (the source products document URL ingestion, 9:16 projects and source-aware generation).
2. Rebuild the prospect’s automatic first pass: select a highlight, create a short scene sequence, apply background removal/reframe/denoise, add a voice or music bed, and generate stylized captions; show a preview and a human “approve/edit” checkpoint rather than pretending the result is final.
3. Rebuild the prospect’s editor surface as canvas/preview above a simple multitrack timeline with video, still, voice, music, caption and overlay tracks. Let a user edit caption text directly, drag/trim clips, change the hook/CTA, and switch to a transcript view for copy edits.
4. Rebuild the prospect’s output controls: render a 1080×1920 H.264 MP4 with captions burned in, export the same captions as SRT, and save an editable project package. Where the shop uses Jianying/CapCut, also generate the corresponding draft folder/JSON or structured edit plan so the MP4 opens immediately and the draft remains revisable.
5. Rebuild the prospect’s delivery loop: run caption-sync, audio/A-V, dead-air, flicker, framing and B-roll checks; expose the receipt and let the human approve, regenerate or edit.
Lift: make the handoff deterministic and editor-neutral—every successful run must leave MP4+SRT+editable project artifacts, with a fail-closed QA receipt and no watermark on the baseline export.
